doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Ellington, Lunceford and storytelling in music
summary: Ellington and Lunceford's music tells stories, like Strauss's Till Eulenspiegel; he wants to do that through improvisation.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You couldn’t have picked anybody better than Ellington to do that too.

Oh yeah man, because Duke, in Duke’s music, the music was telling the story. You could hear it in the music. You know Jimmie Lunceford too. You know there’s a thing he did on “Stormy Weather” and in Jimmie Lunceford, you could hear the storm. It’s sort of like some of the music of Richard Strauss, he had like programmatic music. You could hear the story in the music. I remember Till Eulenspiegel — you know the story about that — you could hear it even when he goes to the gallows man, it’s all in the music. It says something. So you could hear it in the arrangement. I want to learn how to do that through my improvisation spontaneous. Because I didn’t have the discipline to sit — I’ve written big band music charts but I’ve done a lot of things by head that’s in the classroom. I wanted it quick and fast man.
